extracted.intended_audience: economists, social theorists, and students/readers of Veblen's social-economic analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and characterizing the economic-theory criteria Veblen uses to evaluate how animistic beliefs, anthropomorphic cults, and related habits of mind affect individual and collective industrial serviceability and social institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility in apprehending and adapting to a quantitatively determined causal sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'intelligence' demanded of the workman, as well as of the director of an industrial process, is little else than a degree of facility in the apprehension of and adaptation to a quantitatively determined causal sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facility is required for highest serviceability in modern, large-scale industry; lack of it identifies 'stupid' workmen. Education aimed at industrial efficiency should develop this facility. Example/implication: ability to discriminate and select natural forces to work in man's service; ability declines value of mere dexterity or brute force in mechanized industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from bias in causal apprehension / absence of animistic methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In so far as the individual's inherited aptitudes or his training incline him to account for facts and sequences in other terms than those of causation or matter-of-fact, they lower his productive efficiency or industrial usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animistic biases (accounting for events by propensities, luck, or preternatural agency) interfere with the quantitative-causal thinking required for industrial tasks. This lowering of efficiency is more evident in mass/population scale and grows more important as industry becomes more interconnected and mechanized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree and form of animistic belief (naive animism → anthropomorphic agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Animistic belief ranges from an inchoate instinctive sense of inscrutable propensity in objects to a more articulate belief in a preternatural agency, and further to fully anthropomorphic personification of that agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different forms have differing effects: naive animism is pervasive and affects thinking broadly; anthropomorphic cults may limit application and allow provisional causal reasoning for trivial matters. The degree of personification affects how and when the agent is invoked (e.g., wager of battle as anthropomorphic umpire).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope/breadth of habitual application of animistic formula
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the animistic habit is present in the naive form, its scope and range of application are not defined or limited; it will palpably affect his thinking at every turn of the person's life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If animistic explanations are applied broadly, they more severely blur appreciation of causal sequence and reduce industrial serviceability. If anthropomorphic belief is more specialized, many everyday facts may be provisionally accounted for in causal terms until exigency recalls recourse to the preternatural agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preternatural agency as a recourse in perplexity (non-economic utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The extra-causal propensity or agent has a very high utility as a recourse in perplexity, but its utility is altogether of a non-economic kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While offering psychological refuge, comfort, and moral/aesthetic value, appeal to a preternatural agency does not enhance industrial efficiency and may detract from it when relied on instead of causal analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative/mass effect of animistic habit on collective industrial efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Through its cumulative effect upon the habitual attitude of the population, even a slight or inconspicuous bias towards accounting for everyday facts by recourse to other ground than that of quantitative causation may work an appreciable lowering of the collective industrial efficiency of a community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate not only individual-level beliefs but their prevalence and cumulative impact on the workforce and institutional performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation with predatory/emulative traits, status, and prowess
rubrics_metrics.description: Barbarian peoples with a well-developed predatory scheme of life are commonly also possessed of a strong prevailing animistic habit, a well-formed anthropomorphic cult, and a lively sense of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of animism signals likely co-occurrence of other archaic traits (prowess, emulative comparison, status-consciousness) that jointly shape economic behavior (consumption patterns, labor discipline, social structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthropomorphic cults as conservators of status-regime habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Anthropomorphic cults act to conserve, if not to initiate, habits of mind favorable to a regime of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devout observances and religious rituals reinforce recognition of superior/inferior relations, allegiance, and invidious comparison; these influence tastes, consumption, and social deference—important for economic analysis of institutions and markets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced habitual recognition of relation to a superior (fealty) and its economic consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The animistic habit gives rise in the development of an anthropomorphic cult to a code of devout proprieties which induce and conserve a certain habitual recognition of the relation to a superior, and so stiffen the current sense of status and allegiance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'fealty' is a variant of personal subservience that affects both consumption patterns (prestige goods, ceremonial expenditures) and the social organization of production (deference, obedience), and so should be counted in economic appraisals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual reinforcement of sporting (emulative) temper and devout observances
rubrics_metrics.description: The sporting temperament comprises psychological elements that shade off into the frame of mind which finds gratification in devout observances; habituation to sports acts to develop the propensities which find satisfaction in devout observances, and conversely habituation to devout observances favors the growth of a proclivity for athletic sports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: lay religious organizations (YMCA, Young People's Societies) promote athletics as proselyting/retentive tools; church raffles and bazaars exemplify sanctioned gambling-like practices. When assessing social institutions, note these cross-reinforcing channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of perceived agency moderates behavioral expression (less specific luck vs personal divinity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sporting man's sense of luck is often less specific or integrated than the anthropomorphic divinity; his basis for gambling is an instinctive sense of extraphysical propensity scarcely recognized as a personal agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior differs depending on whether the animistic sense is diffuse (luck/mascot/hoodoo) or personified (divinity): diffuse forms promote gambling and charm-tending, while personified forms encourage ritual propitiation and sustained devout observance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: remoter economic effects are obscure and difficult to trace
rubrics_metrics.description: These remoter effects are very difficult to trace... any attempt to inquire into their economic value must for the present be fruitless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution and humility when attributing long-run economic impacts to religious or animistic beliefs; focus on immediate, tangible effects (work habits, consumption, institutional reinforcement) where causal links are clearer.
